plans.title: YRL floor 1 outside the Research Commons (2016 map)

source.what: Charles E. Young Research Library First Floor Map (2016, before the Research Commons remodel; hosted by UCLA Humanities)

plans.how: Walls are the dark lines of the plan image; rooms are the spaces they enclose, with door gaps closed by extending each wall end up to 2 m. The plan has no scale or north arrow, so its building outline was fitted to the mapped outline (scale, rotation and shift, by iterative closest point).

fit.transform: similarity, plan footprint fitted to the building outline (ICP)

notes: This map is from 2016. The Research Commons part of the floor was remodeled since, so that part comes from the 2024 map; only the rest of the floor is taken from this one.
The spaces from this map were read off it by hand as rectangles; the map is a diagram without real wall lines.

plans.title: Research Commons (west and central part of floor 1)

source.what: "2024 Updated - YRL RC Wall Map", the map on the Research Commons room booking page

plans.how: Rooms are the solid colored blocks of the map; labels were read by OCR and checked by hand. The plan was fitted to the ground with a similarity transform on 4 control points (all-gender restroom 11940 (UCLA GIS); all-gender restroom 11938 (UCLA GIS); all-gender restroom 11368A (UCLA GIS); all-gender restroom 11368B (UCLA GIS)).
notes: The library map is a diagram: corridors are the white space between rooms, not drawn walls.
Which restroom number goes with which pink box is matched by position (west pair = 11938/11940, east pair = 11368A/B).
Gray blocks are areas the map leaves unlabeled.
Pod positions are the centers of the pod tables on the map.
The two small teal boxes next to the restrooms have no label or legend on the map.

plans.title: Young Research Library floor 2 (library floor map)

source.what: "Charles E. Young Research Library Floor Maps" (web edition: schematic block diagrams of floors A, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 with stair, elevator and restroom icons, no room numbers; raster images in a PDF; taken down since, recovered from the Common Crawl 2019-10 capture)

plans.how: Rooms are the solid colored blocks of the map; labels were read by OCR and checked by hand. The plan was fitted to the ground with a affine transform on 4 control points (NW corner of the floor's frame on the map; NE corner of the frame; SE corner of the frame; SW corner of the frame).

control.what: NW corner of the floor's frame on the map

notes: The library map is a block diagram: blue blocks are the spaces it names, white is open floor and corridors, the gray blocks hold the restroom and elevator icons. No room numbers; the stacks blocks are labelled with their call-number ranges as on the map.

The map's rectangular frame is taken as the building envelope (affine fit to the outline's four corners), so shapes are only as good as the diagram. North is up on the map: the restroom/elevator cores sit where UCLA's floor 1 restroom records put them (north half, west and east).

The crop is set 12 px inside the diagram's frame line: the frame's anti-aliased inner edge is neither ink nor paper, so it forms a thin ring region whose hole is the whole floor and the tracer's hole filling then swallows every block inside it. The ink threshold is 130 so the frame itself counts as wall.
The two stair icons' boxes get the stair kind with set; the gray cores are split into restrooms (top) and elevators (bottom).

Each gray block on the map holds the restroom icons in its top half and the elevator icons in its bottom half; a cut across the middle of each block (carried on through the small block attached to the west core's side) separates them and set gives them their kinds.
